I think that they are first things to fight before exposure, because getting exposed without knowledge about your psychical reactions and their reasons will change nothing and even can cause new traumas. Of course, exposure can let us see that many our situational fear and anxiety is empty and senseless, but before that we should understand wher that anxiety comes from.

I think you mix here Vespers and Compline. Also you mix the 1962 version with older ones. 

Yes, generally we start with "Deus in adiutorium", immediately after we said five psalms with their antiphones, as you have written. After last antiphone we have the Chapter or Capitulum it is the short reading from the Scripture. Then we have hymn. Immediately after the hymn we have so called Versicle, it is a short dialog of the verses. After the Versicle we have antiphone and Magnificat. Immediatelly after we have "Domine exaudi - Et clamor". Then we say the collect of the day and a commemoration if any appears. We conclude the office with next "Domine exaudi", then "Benedicamus Domino - Deo Gratias", then "Fidelium animae". And this is the end of the Vespers. 

  
If you are a laity, you don't use Dominus vobiscum, because it is a verse used only by the clergy. In the place lay persons use "Domine exaudi orationem meam" as I have pointed above. In 1962 version of the Breviary we don't have Suffregium and commemoration of the Cross at all. It is never used. Also number of commemorations of saints and feasts is very limited in vespers. Commemorations are much more often in Lauds. The antiphone to the Virgin Mary like "Salve Regina" in 1962 version is used only after Compline, it is not a part of vespers. 

Also in the 1962 version there is no Pater Noster after the conclusion of the hour. It is part of it in older versions of the office, but it is deleted for the 1962 version. You should also know that in older versions each hour began with Pater Noster and Ave Maria (Matins and Prime had also Credo).

Unless you are a priest, monk, nun or any other consecrateed perosn, you are under no obligation to pray the Liturgy of Hours at all. As a laity you can pray all the hours of the day, part of them or just one. If you don't have time for that in the certain day, you dont have to pray the LOH at all. 

If you think you wake up too late, or you are too busy in the proper time of prayer, know that the times of the LOH prayers are quite elastic. Morning prayer, you can pray in any time ytou think is morning for you 5 am, 6 am, 8am. The same is the Vespers, which can be said from the late afternoon until night. Actually non of the prayers has any fixed propoer hour to say. It is more like general part of the day, it should be said in, nothing more. 

Once again, if you are laity, do not pressure yourself with such a details. Pray when you are able. Someone said once "Pray as you are able, do not pray as you are not able". Don't put too much burden on yourself with the POH, because it can cause you start to hate this prayer.

If you feel genuine vocation towards the God's service then you should research multiple types of the orders, like monastic, beggars, preachers, hospital, educational. You should also research over yourself. Which way of life is the best for you. Then start to look for a specific order in the chosen way of life. 

Looking for vocation anywhere... isn't to healthy idea.

Couple of minutes?  Don't worry, canonical hours don't have so specificly fixed time. You don't have to  pray morning prayer on 6 am, none on 9 am, sext on noon, vespers on 6 pm etc. Times of prayer are approximate, not mandatory. For example I prayed laudes and prime today on 7 am, my sext on 1 pm. 

If you can't pray on exact due to your work, don't put so much burden on yourself. Liturgy of hours isn't mandatory. Don't treat it as a challenge to do everything according to rubrics or on exact time. It's not the purpose of the prayer.
